title: Panini's Ashtadhyayi
summary: Panini, a Sanskrit grammarian born at Shalatula near Attock on the Indus, is credited with the Ashtadhyayi, a treatise in eight chapters of just under 4,000 sutras that systematised Sanskrit grammar. His dates are uncertain: experts have proposed anywhere from the 4th to the 7th century BC.

uncertainty.note: MacTutor says the dates "are pure guesses" with experts giving the 4th, 5th, 6th and 7th centuries BC; Learn Sanskrit Online says around the 5th century BCE. 7th century BC = astronomical -699 to -600; 4th century BC = -399 to -300.

as_recorded.value: Experts give dates in the 4th, 5th, 6th and 7th century BC
Pāṇini lived sometime around the 5th century BCE

where.modern_name: Attock area, Punjab, Pakistan (proxy pin: Panini's birthplace Shalatula is "near Attock"; the place of composition is not named)
where.historical_name: Shalatula, near Attock on the Indus (northwest of the Indian subcontinent; no polity named in the sources)

importance.justification: A comprehensive grammar of Sanskrit which MacTutor says fixed the language's general shape for the next two thousand years.

sources.title: Panini (520 BC - 460 BC)
sources.publisher: MacTutor History of Mathematics, University of St Andrews

reviewer_note: Least sure of the date (sources say it is guesswork; the MacTutor page title uses 520-460 BC, but its text says the dates are guesses) and of the place: the pin is a proxy for the birthplace, not the place of composition. Only two real publishers; the second (Learn Sanskrit Online) is a teaching site, class other.
